public_rationale: The claim forecasts that neurosymbolic AI will displace pure LLMs. It is qualified by 'over time', which sets no deadline, so the horizon is open. The packet cites one evidence item, a survey preprint posted on 2025-10-24 (e1). The survey treats symbolic methods as something to integrate into LLMs. It also says there is 'limited systematic understanding' of how to integrate them. This is context and does not show displacement. The packet has no dated primary-source event showing that neurosymbolic systems have replaced pure LLMs as the main approach at leading labs or in leading products. The early-resolution rule is therefore not met. Because the forecast has no deadline, the lack of such evidence as of 2026-10-28 does not contradict it. The claim is unresolved.
limitations: Neither 'neurosymbolic' nor 'pure LLM' is defined. Whether LLMs that use tools or agent harnesses count as neurosymbolic is disputed, and the outcome may depend on that choice.
'Displace' could mean full replacement or only the loss of the dominant position.
The packet has only one evidence item (e1). It predates the claim and is a single survey, not a measure of adoption.
The packet has no data on the flagship architectures of leading labs, product market share, or the share of research output.

statement.excerpt: Neurosymbolic AI will displace pure LLMs over time; here’s why.
statement.document_title: AI Cartoon of The Year — and five (re)readings for 2026

our_interpretation: Plain reading: at some future point, hybrid systems that combine neural networks with explicit symbolic parts (logic, rules, symbolic programs, knowledge structures) will replace pure LLMs as the main approach in leading AI products and research.
'Over time' sets no deadline, so this is an open-horizon forecast.
The claim would be met by broad evidence that leading labs and products have moved from pure LLMs to systems with real symbolic parts. A single paper or niche product would not be enough.
Whether today's LLMs that call tools (code interpreters, agent harnesses) already count as 'neurosymbolic' is disputed. I do not treat tool use alone as a decisive displacement event.
criteria.support_condition: Clear, dated evidence that neurosymbolic systems have become the main approach in leading AI products and research, replacing pure LLMs. Examples: frontier labs describing their flagship systems as neurosymbolic and moving away from pure LLM scaling, or independent surveys showing that neurosymbolic systems lead in deployment and research.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Because there is no deadline, nothing can strictly refute this forecast. In practice it would be contradicted only if neurosymbolic approaches were clearly abandoned, or if pure LLMs stayed dominant over a very long period, beyond any reasonable reading of 'over time'.
